# Browser upload to catalog Asset

_sequence · source: `docs/atlas/views/sequence/upload-to-catalog.yaml`_

How a file chosen in the browser becomes a catalog Asset. The HTTP request only stages bytes and records durable intent; everything after that is derived background work, and the browser follows the ingest receipt until it is terminal.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant n_web as Upload queue (Web)
    participant n_hasher as Hash worker
    participant n_api as AssetHandler
    participant n_staging as Repository staging
    participant n_catalog as Catalog (SQLite)
    participant n_scheduler as Catalog scheduler
    participant n_river as River (QueueDB)
    participant n_materializer as SourceMaterializer
    participant n_scanner as Repository scanner
    participant n_commits as Commit coordinator
    n_web->>n_hasher: fingerprint each file (BLAKE3 + size)
    n_web->>n_api: POST /assets/precheck with hashes
    n_api-->>n_web: known files are marked duplicate and skip transport
    alt small files
        n_web->>n_api: POST /assets/batch (multipart batch)
    else large files
        n_web->>n_api: create session, then POST chunks
    end
    n_api->>n_staging: write bytes into the repository's private staging area
    n_api->>n_api: re-hash staged bytes and validate the media type
    n_api->>n_catalog: one transaction — staging commit + pending ingest receipt
    n_api-->>n_web: receipt_id per file (#quot;processing#quot;)
    n_web->>n_api: follow receipts (SSE, falls back to polling)
    n_scheduler->>n_catalog: read pending ingest receipts
    n_scheduler->>n_river: insert IngestAssetArgs{CommitID, ReceiptID}
    n_river->>n_materializer: run under the execution governor
    n_materializer->>n_staging: claim commit, verify bytes, move staging file into inbox/
    n_materializer->>n_scanner: bind the on-disk file as known content
    n_scanner->>n_catalog: repository entry + Asset, request analyze/derivatives/transcode/enrich
    n_river->>n_commits: acknowledge the ingest receipt
    n_commits->>n_catalog: receipt becomes terminal#59; wake the scheduler
    n_api-->>n_web: terminal status for every receipt — refresh asset queries
    Note over n_scheduler,n_river: The requested stages are now pending desired state#59; the scheduler derives their River jobs on the next pass (see Background work).
```

## Why the request never does the work

The HTTP handler's only durable effect is one catalog transaction that records the staged file and a pending receipt. If the Server, River, or QueueDB dies afterwards, the next scheduler pass derives the same ingest job again from the catalog. Nothing is lost and nothing runs twice past the commit coordinator's fences.

## Identity

The browser fingerprint is only a precheck hint. The server re-hashes the staged bytes, and the materializer re-verifies them before the move, so the catalog identity (full BLAKE3 + size) never trusts the client.
